note: Create the sync trigger function: on INSERT fill whichever of amount/total is missing from the other; on UPDATE copy whichever one changed to the other. No table lock needed.

In one short transaction: add nullable column total (metadata only, no rewrite), attach the sync trigger, and add a NOT VALID check (total IS NOT NULL) so new rows are already enforced. Takes the table lock with a 200 ms lock_timeout and retries, so app queries never queue behind it for long.
Backfill total = amount for existing rows in batches of 20,000 ids, committing after each batch (short row locks, no long transaction). New rows are already filled by the trigger.
Safety net: fill any row still missing total (should be none).
Validate the check constraint. Scans the table under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes.
Make total NOT NULL. The validated check lets Postgres skip the full-table scan, so the exclusive lock is momentary; then drop the now-redundant check. Lock taken with lock_timeout + retry.
Switch the app to read and write total. During the rolling update old pods write amount and new pods write total; the trigger keeps both columns identical, so every pod reads correct values.
